items.use: Three task columns floating on near-black, the subject inset bottom-left in a rounded window, three pill bars turning green as work completes.
items.steal: The ground is a product UI, not a backdrop: the interface IS the set. Subject never larger than a fifth of the frame. Green carries progress, never decoration.

items.use: A serif headline ('Your brain's context window') over a row of ten rounded bars grading green to red.
items.steal: One serif sentence carries the whole idea; a single row of shapes proves it. This is the house move: claim in serif, evidence as geometry.

items.use: A screenshot of a real post, with orange marker highlights and hand-drawn white arrows labelled 'Works' and 'Looks'.
items.steal: Annotation as argument: two arrows and two words explain a product decision. Orange only on the two phrases that matter.

items.use: Subject in a rounded window on the left third; a full dark dashboard mock on the right with an orange sun mark above it.
items.steal: The most reusable layout in the set: person left, live-looking artefact right, dotted texture in the lower third to stop the black going flat.

items.use: 'Personal intelligence agents' in serif, subtitle in sans, a monitor outline with three check-marked rows and a white circle with a pause glyph.
items.steal: Thin white line icons at one weight, one green tick repeated three times. The pause circle is a character, not an icon — a small mascot earns warmth.

items.use: The same dashboard again, now carrying an orange 'AI-powered' badge, an ask bar and the words 'LLM-powered' set huge under it.
items.steal: Repeat the artefact and add one element: the difference between the two frames IS the explanation. Accent used once per frame.

items.use: 'Projects' in serif over a cloud outline containing an orange sun mark, three crab-glyph nodes and a laptop outline below.
items.steal: A diagram is allowed to be friendly. Two stroke weights (blue cloud, white laptop), orange kept for the brand mark only.

items.use: A mock handwritten note showing HTML/CSS next to a torn-paper 'Video model' card with a red X, plus a green check on 'Much cheaper'.
items.steal: When the argument is a comparison, leave the interface entirely: paper, marker, torn edge. Tactile beats polished for one beat, then back.

items.use: Six app icons in a 3×2 grid with names under them, on black, subject still at left.
items.steal: Icons as evidence in a taxonomy frame. Nothing else on screen: no paragraph, no bullet, no arrow. The grid is the sentence.

items.use: The subject alone, full frame, real room, real window, hands moving, no graphics at all.
items.steal: The reset shot. After five designed frames, one honest one buys back trust — and it is free to produce.
